subject: Pricing & token economics - post-call recap / confirming budget owner
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Pricing & token economics - post-call recap

Thanks again for the time today, Sam — really helpful to understand the integration plan and expected usage. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Usage profile: you mentioned ~8M tokens/day initially, ramping to ~25M tokens/day in Q1. I asked for clarification on peak concurrency and average sequence lengths; attached is a simple forecast we discussed (Acme_token_forecast_2026Q4.xlsx).
- Target unit economics: you called out a target of ~$800 / 1M tokens as a goal for total hosted cost (including caching/batching assumptions).
- Budget & approvals: you said procurement prefers to work with a named budget owner and that Jordan is driving vendor evaluation/finance signoff. Can you confirm?
- Next steps (from Redwood): we can prepare a pricing proposal scoped to your forecast and include a recommended batching/cache profile + pilot discount. Before we do: we need confirmation on (1) expected committed monthly token volume (2) who the economic buyer is and (3) whether finance needs a procurement SOW or PO before signature.

If you can confirm the three items above, I’ll pull together the pricing proposal and a one-page pilot SOW for review. Proposed timeline: draft proposal by Mon 11/30, sign-off by 12/10 to kick off a January pilot.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: Acme_token_forecast_2026Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pricing & token economics - post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications: 

- Volumes: the 8M/day is conservative; realistic ramp is 15M/day by mid-Q1 and 25M/day by end of Q1, ~750M tokens/month at full ramp. Peak concurrency will be moderate; average seq length around 350 tokens.
- Unit economics: finance has indicated a target of ~$800 / 1M tokens for total hosted costs; Jordan and I will push for lower if possible.
- Budget owner & sign-off: Jordan Lee (cc’d) is the primary budget owner and will own finance sign-off. I’m copying him to confirm timing.

Jordan — can you confirm budget timeline? We’re hoping to start a pilot in January.

Best,
Sam

On Thu, Nov 26, 2026 at 15:12, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today, Sam — really helpful to understand the integration plan and expected usage. Quick recap and proposed next steps: ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Pricing & token economics - post-call recap / confirm economic buyer + finance ask

Looping you both in — Sam confirmed volumes and named Jordan Lee as budget owner. Before I draft the external proposal (Redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf), two asks: 

1) Pricing: given the forecast (~750M/mo at full ramp) and target ~ $800 / 1M tokens from the customer, would we recommend a starter list price at $780 / 1M tokens with a pilot discount of 10% for the first 90 days? That nets ~$702 / 1M for the pilot and puts us slightly below their target while protecting revenue on ramp. Please call out any margin/ops concerns.

2) Procurement path: confirm whether we need an SOW before signature or if a standard PO with our T&Cs is OK. Customer hinted procurement may ask for a sample SOW. If they need SOC2 artifacts or contract redlines, loop Legal (not included here).

3) Approver: can you confirm who on the Redwood side should be the owner for pricing escalation/approval for anything below a 15% discount? I’d like to have that named before I share pricing externally.

I’ve attached the draft proposal — happy to iterate. If you’re good, I’ll send to Jordan and Sam with a tight ask for confirmation by 12/10.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing & token economics - post-call recap / confirm economic buyer + finance ask

Thanks Marissa — good plan. Quick responses: 

1) Pricing posture: $780 / 1M as list for the customer is fine given the volume profile. Approve a 10% pilot discount (net $702 / 1M) for 90 days. If they commit to a 6-month minimum or $X reserved capacity, we can discuss stepped discounts after pilot. Ops/infra cost looks acceptable at that rate with current batching/caching assumptions.

2) Procurement: procurement will likely want an SOW for pilots; include a one-page SOW that defines pilot scope, success criteria, and data handling. Standard PO after pilot is fine. Legal should be looped if they ask for contract redlines.

3) Approver: I (aditya_rao) will own pricing escalation approvals up to 15% discount. Anything larger routes to VP Sales.

Please proceed to send the proposal to Jordan and Sam with the pilot terms. I’ll be available to join a call with Jordan if needed.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
